author: Contributor 29
about: Trellis, a four-person product in Lisbon where design agencies collect their clients' feedback, signs its people in with Clerk for 2026: the instance's permissions and roles, a JWT template for Convex, a webhook endpoint, two agencies made on sign-up, invitations sent, revoked and accepted through their tickets, a role changed, a monthly metrics script, a plan in an agency's metadata read by its tokens, a member removed and deleted, an agency renamed and grown, and an agency and its owner leaving. Marta also signs in to Volter Editor through the account worker public-client PKCE request, sees Clerk sign-in and consent, exchanges the code and refreshes the grant.

steps.name: Monday 5 January, 09:00: Inês sets up Trellis's Clerk application
Inês previews the empty development instance; Clerk establishes its development browser
The preview reports its localhost origin to the development environment
The preview fetches the frontend public keys for token verification

On the production instance's dashboard's User & authentication page Inês offers passwords and emailed codes, has sign-up ask people to accept Trellis's terms, and on the Domains page the instance's Frontend API is clerk.trellis.app
On the API Keys page she makes her own secret key, shown once
…and the API server's key, which goes into the server's configuration
The server's setup script, kept under version control, turns Organizations on
On the dashboard's Organizations Settings page Inês chooses membership optional, since Trellis makes each agency itself when its owner onboards
The server's setup script declares the permission "Manage projects"
The server's setup script declares the permission "Edit projects"
The server's setup script declares the permission "Request reviews"
The server's setup script declares the permission "Manage billing"
It makes the contributor role (edit projects, request reviews), in the initial role set so agencies can assign it
…and the viewer role, with no permissions of Trellis's
It looks up Clerk's admin role by its key
…and gives the admin role "manage projects"
…and gives the admin role "edit projects"
…and gives the admin role "request reviews"
…and gives the admin role "manage billing"
With her own key Inês's part of the script makes the convex JWT template: audience convex, and the active agency's plan (the session-tokens page documents org.public_metadata)
Inês registers the private reporting service’s shared-key JWT template
On the Webhooks page she points an endpoint for user.deleted at Trellis's receiver and copies its signing secret into the server's configuration
The API server boots and fetches the instance's public keys, to verify session tokens itself
Inês registers the account worker public OAuth client through Clerk before enabling Editor sign-in
Her setup reads back the registered public OAuth application
The anonymous preview reaches the API; the SDK requests cookies clearing any prior login
The API applies the anonymous handshake directives
Wednesday 7 January, 10:00
Marta opens trellis.app/sign-up; Clerk's sign-up form loads the instance's settings
Marta's new browser has only Trellis's theme cookie; Clerk reads an anonymous client
Clerk's browser SDK establishes Marta's client before signup
She signs up with her work email, her name, and Trellis's terms accepted
Clerk emails her a code
She reads the code in her inbox
Marta is called away before entering the email code
The code she found is now expired; Clerk keeps signup incomplete
She requests a fresh code
She reads the fresh delivery
She mistypes the fresh code once
She types the code; her account is made and she is signed in
Marta reloads the browser; Clerk reads the client and its completed signup session
Trellis's onboarding asks for her agency's name; the API server creates Oak & Ash with Marta as its creator and the trial plan
Onboarding done, the API server marks it in Marta's public metadata, which Trellis's app reads to skip the tour
The API reads Marta for the account header
Marta’s browser loads the avatar URL Clerk returned
Marta's browser switches to Oak & Ash
Her board connects to Convex with a convex token
Marta opens Trellis’s private report; Clerk issues its shared-key audience token
Trellis's API receives Marta's browser without a usable app-domain session cookie; the SDK starts its nonce handshake
The API server exchanges the nonce for the cookies Clerk asks it to set
The account worker's newer SDK asks the default signed handshake when Marta opens Editor
Marta opens Editor sign-in; the worker forwards its authorize URL through the documented Clerk Frontend API proxy
Clerk presents its sign-in page over the same frontend proxy
The sign-in page loads the pinned unmodified clerk-js browser bundle through the worker frontend proxy
Marta uses her signed-in Clerk browser; the worker authorize request now requires consent
The consent page names the account worker and its requested scopes
Marta grants the requested access for Oak & Ash; Clerk redirects to the worker callback with code and preserved state
The worker exchanges its provider code and S256 verifier at the instance custom Frontend API domain
Marta shares a board with an outside reviewer through the account worker
She shares the board with a second outside reviewer through the same worker
The pending-reviewer list orders its newest invitation first
The application reads its pending reviewer invitation
The administrator’s invitation script omits the force flag and refuses a duplicate pending reviewer
Monday 2 February, 08:00: the first metrics run
The reviewer never used the one-day collaboration link; Clerk now returns it expired
Marta reopens Editor; the worker renews her expired access token with the stored refresh token
Inês makes the metrics script's key on the API Keys page, kept on her laptop only
The metrics export sorts January's users by name for its CSV
Its first creation-ordered page closes at Marta
The next export page starts after Marta and is empty
The script looks up January's one new agency admin by the email in Trellis's database
…and reads her sessions to count the devices she came back on
…counts everyone who signed up in January, for the month's report
…and lists the agencies with their sizes
Wednesday 4 February, 11:00
In Trellis's settings Marta invites Rui as a contributor; the API server creates the invitation with Trellis's accept page as its redirect
…and Beatriz, typing her address wrong
The settings page lists the agency's pending invitations, and Marta sees the typo
Marta opens the typoed invitation's details before revoking it
The setup script names Clerk admin as creator and contributors as the domain enrollment default
Trellis calls contributors designers; the setup updates the role key while the designers' invitations are pending
The enrollment default follows the renamed role
Rui's pending invitation follows the renamed designer role
She revokes it
The mistyped recipient opens the old invitation after Marta revoked it
The delivered link refuses the now-revoked invitation
…and invites the right address
That afternoon
Rui, who messaged Marta earlier that he could not find his invitation, finds it in his promotions folder and opens it
He clicks its link; Clerk takes the invitation and sends him on to Trellis's accept page
The link lands on Trellis's accept page, which signs him up through the invitation with his name and the terms accepted
Beatriz opens hers
…and clicks its link
…and signs up the same way

Marta, who read Rui's message that he could not find his invitation, clicks Resend on it in Trellis's settings; Trellis resends by revoking the invitation and inviting again, and Clerk refuses the revoke: Rui found the mail and joined in the meantime
Before she leaves that afternoon Marta opens Oak & Ash's members page, which the API server renders, to see both designers landed
Marta sorts the agency members by first_name
Marta sorts the agency members by last_name
Marta sorts the agency members by username
Marta sorts the agency members by email_address
Marta sorts the agency members by phone_number
Marta sorts the agency members by created_at
Tuesday 10 March, 15:00
Daniel, who runs Northlight in Madrid, signs up
Daniel resumes the signup form after closing the tab
He corrects his displayed name; password and consent are still missing
Clerk emails him a code
He reads it
Daniel verifies his email; Clerk still needs his password and terms accepted
He adds his password and accepts Trellis's terms; Clerk makes his account and session
The API server creates Northlight with Daniel as its creator, on the trial plan
Thursday 12 March, 10:00
Rui opens the signup tab on his new device although his account already exists
Rui opens Trellis on a new device and identifies his account
The form reloads Rui's pending sign-in
Rui mistypes his password
He enters the correct password
Rui's earlier email-code form reaches Clerk after his password sign-in completed; the factor is already verified
Rui asks to change Oak & Ash's billing; the API server reads his memberships and finds his role holds no billing permission, so Trellis refuses him
Monday 16 March, 09:30
Marta makes Beatriz an admin from Trellis's settings, through the API server, so she can manage billing while Marta is away
Monday 6 April, 08:00: the April metrics run
The April CSV orders its four people by first name
The creation-ordered export puts the newest person first
The metrics export takes March's agency administrator and excludes January's
The metrics export filters by the same agencies and orders by email
The script looks up March's one new agency admin, Daniel
…and reads his sessions
…and counts March's sign-ups
Tuesday 14 April, 11:00
Oak & Ash pays for the team plan through Trellis's payment provider; the API server merges it into the agency's public metadata
That afternoon
Beatriz signs in to Trellis with her email
Clerk emails her a code
She reads it (below her invitation)
…and types it
Her browser opens Oak & Ash
Her board reconnects to Convex, and its token reads the team plan
That evening
Beatriz left her laptop on the train; on her phone's browser she signs in to Trellis with her email
She reads it on her phone
Beatriz reaches the train’s lost-property desk before submitting the phone code
Her delayed phone code has expired
She requests a fresh code on the same phone sign-in
She reads the fresh phone delivery
She corrects a mistyped phone code
…and types it
The phone's Clerk SDK reads the session after sign-in
Trellis's phone API requests use the standard session bearer token
Trellis's security page on her phone, through the API server, lists her active sessions: the phone's and the laptop's
…and she signs the laptop's session out
The following morning Beatriz reopens her old security tab, whose device list predates the revocation
The stale security tab still offers the lost laptop; its second revocation is refused
Her security page reloads the remaining active phone before she resets the password
Beatriz changes her password after the lost laptop; a short entry is refused
Using her email address as the replacement password is refused
She saves a new password and ends every remaining active session
The security page now finds no active Beatriz device
Monday 4 May, 10:00
Trellis lets viewers ask for reviews: the server's setup script gives the viewer role "request reviews"
Boards reconnected every minute as their tokens ran out, so with her own key Inês's part of the script sends the convex template again, whole, with an hour's lifetime
Beatriz, married in April, asks Trellis to change her last name; its profile page saves it through the API server
The profile reads the verified primary address before saving her account identity
Her profile adopts her married username and keeps the selected verified primary address
Monday 15 June, 10:00
Rui leaves Oak & Ash; Beatriz removes him in Trellis's settings, through the API server
Rui's old board still selects Oak & Ash; its next token request is refused because he has left
Wednesday 8 July, 14:00
Between agencies Rui helped Northlight; Daniel adds him as a member through Trellis's API server
Rui asks Trellis to delete his account; the API server deletes his user
Deleting Rui's account also removes his remaining Northlight membership
Clerk posts user.deleted to Trellis's receiver, which removes his name from his comments
Monday 7 September, 09:00
Trellis adds agency URL slugs; Inês enables them before the renamed agency chooses its URL
The agency renames itself Oak & Ash Studio and its plan now allows ten members; the API server updates the organization
Oak & Ash Studio's new IT lead wants its people to sign in with their Okta; the API server makes an enterprise connection (SAML, Okta) for the agency's domain
The IT lead first points Clerk at Trellis's uploaded IdP export, but the upload server is unavailable
The uploaded export still lacks its signing certificate; Clerk names the missing field
Once the IT lead uploads the full Okta export to Trellis, the server sets its metadata URL and activates SAML
The server reads the known SAML child back after enterprise configuration, the object a root refresh observes
Monday 28 September, 11:00
The prerelease phone cannot start its Clerk client until Inês enables the Native API
Trellis's iPhone app is ready for the App Store; on the dashboard's Native applications page Inês enables the Native API, which the app needs to use Clerk
…and registers the app, with its App ID prefix and bundle ID
Monday 5 October, 10:00
Trellis ships its iPhone app and emails each agency's people a link that opens it signed in; for Beatriz's link the API server makes a sign-in token that opens Oak & Ash Studio
Before her first app sign-in, the native SDK establishes its client
Beatriz taps the link on her phone; the app, a native client, signs her in with the token and keeps the client token Clerk answers in the Authorization header
Her board in the app connects to Convex with a convex token carrying the team plan
Inês registers the Google OAuth client used by Editor’s advertised Google sign-in
Nuno’s Google account is the identity he chooses when he joins Marta’s Editor session
Inês enters the Google client credentials on Clerk’s social connections page
The shared-session sign-in loads the environment and displays its Google button
Nuno’s new browser establishes its Clerk client before choosing Google
Nuno tries Google but declines its permission prompt
Google returns the declined consent to Clerk; the callback goes back to the sign-in page
The SDK reloads the failed sign-in and shows the provider refusal
Nuno chooses Google, then is interrupted while the provider page is open
Nuno’s first Google sign-in; his browser opens Google’s account chooser
Nuno’s first Google sign-in; he chooses his Google account and consents
The shared laptop is idle for eleven minutes before Nuno completes the return
After eleven minutes he returns to the provider callback; Clerk reports the expired verification
The callback page reloads the expired verification and asks him to start again
Nuno returns to the shared-session link and chooses Google again
Nuno’s first Google sign-in; his browser opens Google’s account chooser
Nuno’s first Google sign-in; he chooses his Google account and consents
Nuno’s first Google sign-in; Google returns the code to Clerk and Clerk exchanges it at Google’s token endpoint
Clerk’s callback page reloads the transferable sign-in for a first-time account
The pinned SDK transfers the Google identity into signup, with its address already verified
Nuno accepts the displayed terms; signup completes without asking the Google user for a password
Nuno leaves the shared laptop using SignIn’s sign-out-all control; Clerk removes its sessions and retains the client cookie
Nuno reopens Editor’s shared-session link and signs into his existing account with Google
Nuno’s returning Google sign-in; his browser opens Google’s account chooser
Nuno’s returning Google sign-in; he chooses his Google account and consents
Nuno’s returning Google sign-in; Google returns the code to Clerk and Clerk exchanges it at Google’s token endpoint
Clerk’s callback page reloads the completed sign-in and its session for the existing account
Monday 9 November, 10:00
Daniel tells Trellis Northlight is closing; the API server deletes the organization
Daniel, who has no other agency, asks Trellis to delete his account; the API server deletes his user
Clerk posts user.deleted, and the receiver removes his records
